texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is barely grown and all elbows, and has walked up from {PLACE} with a letter from {X_possessive} family and a purse of {COUNT} silver for board. They want {X_objective} taught a trade, and the talk in {PLACE} is that the best hands at a bench for a day's walk belong to {A_nameDef}.\n\n{X_nameDef} would come up a day or two each week through the season and work at {A_nameDef}'s side.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}'s mother sent {X_objective} up from {PLACE} with a basket of eggs, a purse of {COUNT} silver and a speech learned by heart: {FACTION} have no one with {A_nameDef}'s skill, and {X_nameDef} is good with {X_possessive} hands and bad at sitting still. Would {A_nameDef} take {X_objective} on for the season?

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has the family's letter in one hand and a dented toolbox in the other. The workshops in {PLACE} aren't taking apprentices this year, the letter says, and {A_nameDef}'s work is spoken of there.\n\nThere's {COUNT} silver for {X_possessive} keep, if the colony will have {X_objective} at the bench a day or two a week until the season turns.

[colony:Hardworking] They say in {PLACE} that the colony works from dark to dark, and {X_nameDef}'s family thinks that's exactly what {X_nameDef} needs. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up with {COUNT} silver for board, to learn a trade at {A_nameDef}'s elbow through the season, and looks as if {X_pronoun} would rather be anywhere else.

li.label: Take {X_objective} on, and the board money ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took the purse and the letter, and spent the afternoon showing {X_nameDef} round the workshop: what to touch, what never to touch, where the broom is. {X_nameDef} will be back next week.

li.label: Take {X_objective} on, and send the silver back
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} pressed the purse back into {X_nameDef}'s hands for the family and showed {X_objective} round the workshop instead. The family at {PLACE} will hear about the purse before they hear anything else.

li.label: {A_nameDef} has no time for a pupil
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took the letter back, folded it carefully along its old creases, and went home to {PLACE}.

coming.li: [apprenticebench] {X_nameDef}, the apprentice from {PLACE}, starts at {A_nameDef}'s bench within {DAYS}.
[apprenticetrouble] {X_nameDef} is learning the trade at {A_nameDef}'s bench, up from {PLACE} a day or two each week. Due again within {DAYS}.
[apprenticepiece] {X_nameDef} is making a piece to show what the season taught. Due within {DAYS}.
[guild] {X_nameDef}'s family is settling things with the guild at {PLACE}. Word within {DAYS}.

endings.li: [joined] {X_nameDef} has a bed at the colony now, and a place at {A_nameDef}'s bench that is {X_possessive} own. The family at {PLACE} sent {X_possessive} things up on a cart, with a letter that was mostly about socks.
[joined,piece] {X_nameDef} lives at the colony now. The stool with the short leg still stands by {A_nameDef}'s bench, and {X_nameDef} has offered twice to fix it. {A_nameDef} won't let {X_objective}.

[journeyman] {X_nameDef} is home at {PLACE} with a journeyman's skill and a set of the colony's old tools, and the family has sent something up the road by way of thanks: {ITEM}.\n\nThere's already talk at {PLACE} of a workshop of {X_possessive} own.

[journeyman,free] {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} a journeyman. The family remembered the purse the colony sent back in the spring, and the gift that came up the road afterward is worth far more than the purse was: {ITEM}.
[journeyman,greedy] {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} a journeyman, and the family sent their thanks: {ITEM}. They have also told the market they paid twice for the timber, more than once.

[guild] {X_nameDef} has gone to the guild at {PLACE}, with wages and a bed and a master who doesn't know {X_objective} yet. A small package came up the road for {A_nameDef} afterward: {ITEM}, and a note in careful letters that says thank you.

[guild,family] The family chose the guild, as families do. {X_nameDef} went, and wrote to {A_nameDef} from {PLACE}: the guild's bench is wider, the master is stricter, and {X_nameDef} misses the colony's. A gift came with the letter: {ITEM}.

[home] {X_nameDef} is home at {PLACE}, where {X_pronoun} wanted to be. The family let the colony know they're grateful, and that {X_nameDef} talks about {A_nameDef}'s workshop more than they expected.

[drifted] {X_nameDef} never came back up the hill. The family at {PLACE} wrote to say sorry, and that {X_nameDef} has taken up with a crowd at the market they don't like. {A_nameDef} cleared {X_possessive} things off the bench without saying anything.

[drifted,greedy] {X_nameDef} never came back up the hill, and the family at {PLACE} wrote to say the timber money is gone too. {A_nameDef} cleared {X_possessive} things off the bench and put the half-made pieces on the woodpile.
[declined] {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} and took work at the tannery. The family doesn't hold it against the colony. Not much.
[lost] Word stopped coming up from {PLACE}. A trader thought {X_nameDef}'s family had moved on, and taken {X_objective} with them.

summaries.li: [joined] {X_nameDef} came from {PLACE} to learn a trade at {A_nameDef}'s bench, and stayed.
[journeyman] The colony taught {X_nameDef} of {PLACE} a trade for a season and sent {X_objective} home a journeyman.
[guild] The apprentice {X_nameDef} left the colony's bench for the guild at {PLACE}.
[home] The apprentice {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} before the season was out.
[drifted] The apprentice {X_nameDef} drifted away from the colony's bench.
[declined] The colony turned down an apprentice from {PLACE}.

texts.li: [gifted] {X_nameDef} is back up from {PLACE} for the week, and has already made a joint that {A_nameDef} had to look at twice. Cleaner than {A_nameDef}'s own were at that age, {A_nameDef} admits, though not to {X_nameDef}.\n\nThe question is what to do with a quick pair of hands.

[homesick] {X_nameDef} works hard at {A_nameDef}'s bench and says very little, and every hour or so looks down the road toward {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} in the woodshed yesterday with red eyes, blaming the sawdust.\n\nIt's {X_possessive} first time away from home.

[restless] In {X_nameDef}'s first week at the bench: one saw blade snapped, one chisel lost, and an afternoon spent up on the roof watching a hawk. {A_nameDef} says the hands are good, when they stay on the work.\n\n{X_nameDef} is back up from {PLACE} today, grinning.

li.label: Keep {X_objective} at {A_nameDef}'s elbow all day
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} kept {X_nameDef} at the bench from breakfast to supper, hands on the tools and eyes on {A_nameDef}'s hands.

outcomes.li: [gifted] {A_nameDef} kept {X_nameDef} at the bench all day, and by evening {X_nameDef} was showing {A_nameDef} a faster way to cut a mortise. {A_nameDef} let {X_objective}.
[homesick] {A_nameDef} kept {X_nameDef} so busy at the bench that {X_nameDef} only looked down the road twice all day.
[restless] {A_nameDef} kept {X_nameDef} at the bench until supper, and {X_nameDef} got through the whole day without breaking anything, which {A_nameDef} counts as a good day.

li.label: Set {X_objective} a piece of {X_possessive} own to make
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spent the day on a stool, start to finish, and handed it to {A_nameDef} with both hands. One leg is short. {A_nameDef} is keeping it anyway.

outcomes.li: [gifted] {X_nameDef} made a stool from start to finish without asking a single question, and none of its legs is short. {A_nameDef} looked at it for a long time.

li.label: Ask {X_possessive} family for more, for the timber
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} brought the family's answer up the next morning: half as much again, for timber, and a note saying they hoped the work was worth it.

texts.li: [gifted] A master of the guild at {PLACE} has seen {X_nameDef}'s work and offered to take {X_objective} on: wages, a bed, and a guild mark at the end of it. {X_nameDef}'s family wants the guild.\n\n{X_nameDef} came up today to say so, and to say {X_pronoun} would rather finish the season with {A_nameDef}.

[gifted,piece] Word of the stool got round {PLACE}, and a master of the guild there came to look at {X_nameDef}'s hands and offered {X_objective} a place: wages, a bed, a mark of {X_possessive} own one day. The family is ready to say yes. {X_nameDef} wants to stay at {A_nameDef}'s bench.

[homesick] {X_nameDef} came up from {PLACE} today with a bundle of {X_possessive} things, to say goodbye. The work is good, {X_nameDef} says, and {A_nameDef} is kind, and {X_nameDef} can't stand being away from home another week.

[restless] {X_nameDef} missed last week at the bench, and turned up today with mud to the knees and a story that changes every time it's told. Word from {PLACE} is that {X_nameDef} has been spending the days at the market with a crowd the family doesn't like.

[restless,greedy] {X_nameDef}'s family paid twice for timber, and {X_nameDef} hasn't been near the bench in a week. Today {X_nameDef} turned up with mud to the knees and a story that keeps changing. The family at {PLACE} will want to know where their silver went.

li.label: {A_nameDef} has a long talk with {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took {X_nameDef} out to the woodpile and talked, and mostly listened, until the light went. {X_nameDef} will be at the bench next week.

outcomes.li: [gifted] {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} the guild would still be there in spring, and the season wasn't over. {X_nameDef}'s family grumbled, and agreed to wait.
[homesick] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} talked until dark about home, mostly {X_nameDef}'s. {X_nameDef} unpacked the bundle and stayed for supper.
[restless] {A_nameDef} didn't shout. {A_nameDef} handed {X_nameDef} the hardest job in the workshop and stood over it until it was done right, and the next week {X_nameDef} came up on time.

li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} talked until the light went, and {X_nameDef} listened politely, and at the end of it nothing had changed.

riskOutcomes.li: [gifted] {A_nameDef} talked until the light went. {X_nameDef} cried, and is going to the guild.
[homesick] {A_nameDef} talked until the light went, and in the morning {X_nameDef} picked up the bundle and went home.
[restless] {A_nameDef} talked until the light went, and {X_nameDef} nodded at all of it and went off toward {PLACE} without looking back.

li.label: Write to {X_possessive} family at {PLACE}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} wrote to the family at {PLACE} and sent the letter down with {X_nameDef}.

outcomes.li: [gifted] {A_nameDef} wrote to the family. They wrote back that the guild is a chance {X_nameDef} won't get twice, and they aren't wrong.
[homesick] {A_nameDef} wrote to the family, and they wrote back: a week at home, and then {X_nameDef} goes back up to finish what {X_pronoun} started.
[restless] {A_nameDef} wrote to the family, and {X_nameDef}'s father came up from {PLACE} the next day with {X_nameDef} beside him, to apologize to {A_nameDef} in person.

li.label: Let {X_objective} go, with thanks
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} shook {X_nameDef}'s hand at the gate and said the bench would be there if {X_pronoun} ever wanted it.

texts.li: The season is nearly over, and {X_nameDef} has come up from {PLACE} with something under a blanket: a piece made start to finish, to show {A_nameDef} what the season taught. {X_nameDef} is too nervous to take the blanket off.\n\nAfter today, {X_nameDef} goes home a journeyman, unless the colony gives {X_objective} a reason not to.

[gifted] {X_nameDef} has made a chair. Not a stool, not a box: a chair, with a carved back and joints {A_nameDef} has to look at twice. {X_nameDef} brought it up from {PLACE} on a borrowed handcart to show {A_nameDef}, and to ask what comes next.
[homesick,family] A week at home did {X_nameDef} good. {X_nameDef} came back to finish the season, and today brought up the piece {X_pronoun} has been making in the evenings, to show {A_nameDef}.

[restless,family] Since {X_possessive} father came up the hill, {X_nameDef} hasn't missed a day. Today {X_nameDef} brought a piece up from {PLACE}, made at home in the evenings, and set it down in front of {A_nameDef} without a word.
[piece] The first thing {X_nameDef} made at the colony was a stool with one short leg. Today {X_nameDef} brought up a chair, and none of its legs is short.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay on, as one of the colony
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} looked the piece over for a long time, then asked {X_nameDef} to stay. {X_nameDef} said yes before {A_nameDef} had finished asking.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} asked {X_nameDef} to stay. {X_nameDef} wanted to, and said so, and said no: there's a family at {PLACE} that needs {X_objective} more.

li.label: Send {X_objective} home a journeyman
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} kept the piece and gave {X_nameDef} a set of the colony's old tools to take home. A few of the colony walked {X_objective} to the gate, and {A_nameDef} went furthest.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} got as far as the colony's gate and sat down against the post, burning with fever and shivering in the sun. {X_nameDef} was on the way home to {PLACE}, and won't get there like this.\n\n{A_nameDef}, the colony's best doctor, took one look and asked the council to decide quickly.

[lowtech] The traveler at the gate is {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, gray in the face and soaked through, with the kind of fever that takes people on the road. {X_nameDef} asks for nothing but a dry place to lie down.\n\n{A_nameDef} says a fever like that can turn either way, and it may be catching.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came off the road in the rain and went down by the gate, with a temperature {A_nameDef} didn't like and a cough that sounds deep. The nearest proper clinic is days away at {PLACE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} can treat it here, if the council agrees.

[winter] Snow on {X_possessive} shoulders and fever in {X_possessive} face: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} won't last another night on the road to {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} has already fetched a blanket, and is waiting on the council.

li.label: Take {X_objective} in; {A_nameDef} will nurse {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat up with {X_nameDef} through the worst of the night, with cold cloths and the medicine chest open. By morning the fever had broken, or bent at least.

li.label: Medicine and a dry corner by the wall, then on to {PLACE}
li.outcome: A dose of medicine and a blanket went out to {X_nameDef} by the wall, and in the morning {X_nameDef} went on toward {PLACE}, slowly, stopping often.

li.label: Keep {X_objective} away; it may be catching
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} was told to keep away. In the morning the place by the gatepost was empty, and a line of footprints led off toward {PLACE}.

coming.li: [feverrelapse|fevermended] {X_nameDef}, the traveler with the fever, is on the road to {PLACE}. Word of how {X_pronoun} fares should come within {DAYS}.
[feverrepaid] {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} promising the colony would hear from {X_objective} again. Within {DAYS}, perhaps.
[saved|helped|closed] The fever is going through {PLACE}. Word of how the town fares should come within {DAYS}.
[turnedaway] The traveler the colony turned away from its gate is somewhere on the road to {PLACE}. Word may come within {DAYS}.

endingTitles.li: [turnedaway] The traveler the colony turned away

endings.li: [joined] {X_nameDef} sleeps at the colony now, in a bed this time, and works as if the fever owed {X_objective} the weeks it took. {A_nameDef} still checks {X_possessive} forehead now and then, out of habit.

[saved] Word came up from {PLACE}: the fever has run its course, and the medicine the colony sent went where it was needed most. {FACTION} haven't forgotten who sent it, and a gift came up the road afterward: {ITEM}.

[saved,nursed] The fever at {PLACE} is over. {X_nameDef} went from house to house with the colony's medicine and {A_nameDef}'s way of doing things, and there are people walking about at {PLACE} who {FACTION} say wouldn't be. A gift came up the road for the colony: {ITEM}.

[helped] The fever at {PLACE} has burned itself out. {A_nameDef}'s advice went round the town on the back of a feed sack, copied out a dozen times, and {FACTION} credit it with the houses that got off lightly.
[closed] The fever ran its course at {PLACE} without the colony. {X_nameDef} has stopped coming up the road, and {FACTION} remember the shut gate.
[turnedaway] {X_nameDef} reached {PLACE} in the end and pulled through, slowly, in a neighbor's spare bed. {FACTION} know which colony kept its gate shut on a sick traveler, and say so.

[turnedaway,strong] {X_nameDef} shook the fever off on the road and reached {PLACE} on {X_possessive} own feet. {X_nameDef} tells the story of the colony that wouldn't open its gate to anyone who'll listen.
[worse] {X_nameDef} mended in the end, at {PLACE}, over a long hard month. {FACTION} remember that the colony helped once, and then didn't.
[lost] No more word came up the road about {X_nameDef}. A trader thought the traveler with the fever had gone south to family, and that was the last anyone heard.

summaries.li: [joined] {X_nameDef}, a traveler the colony nursed through a fever, stayed.
[saved] The colony's medicine saw {PLACE} through the fever {X_nameDef} first brought to its gate.
[closed] The colony kept its gate shut while a fever went through {PLACE}.
[turnedaway] The colony turned away {X_nameDef}, a traveler with a fever.
[worse] The colony helped a feverish traveler once, and then stopped.
[lost] A traveler the colony helped through a fever was never heard of again.

texts.li: [relapse] {X_nameDef} came back up the road on a borrowed mule, gray and shaking. The fever came back two days out of {PLACE}, worse than before, and the healer there sent {X_objective} straight back: go to the one who treated you.

[lingering] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is mending, but so slowly that the family at {PLACE} has given up waiting. {X_nameDef} walked back up to the colony leaning on a stick, to ask {A_nameDef} what else can be done.

[relapse,sent] Last time, the colony gave {X_nameDef} medicine and a corner outside the wall. The fever came back on the road, and {X_nameDef} is at the gate again, worse, asking for more than a corner this time.

[lingering,nursed] {A_nameDef} pulled {X_nameDef} through the first night, but the fever never quite let go. {X_nameDef} has come back up from {PLACE} thin and slow, to see the doctor who started the job.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sits with {X_objective} again (2 medicine)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat with {X_nameDef} another long night and went through two doses from the medicine chest. Near dawn the fever let go, for good this time, {A_nameDef} thinks.

li.label: Medicine for the road (2)
li.outcome: Two doses went out to {X_nameDef} at the gate, wrapped in a cloth with instructions, and {X_nameDef} started back for {PLACE} before dark.

li.label: The colony has done what it can
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nodded, as if expecting it, and started back down the road toward {PLACE}.

texts.li: [nursed] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is back on {X_possessive} own two feet, brown from the road and a good deal thinner. {X_nameDef} remembers very little of the fever and every bit of {A_nameDef} sitting up through it, and has come to say so, and to pay the debt.
[sent] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come back up from {PLACE}, well again. The medicine the colony carried out to the wall did the work, {X_nameDef} says, and {X_pronoun} pays {X_possessive} debts.

[lingering] {X_nameDef} still walks with a stick and still stops on hills, but the fever is gone. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up from {PLACE} to thank {A_nameDef}, and to ask how the colony would like to be repaid.

[strong] Brown from the road and grinning, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is back at the gatepost where {X_pronoun} sat down with the fever a few weeks ago. {X_nameDef} has come to repay the colony, and won't take no for an answer.

li.label: Let {X_objective} work off the debt
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took an axe to the treeline and didn't stop until the light went. There's a good start on the winter's firewood lying where the trees came down, and {X_nameDef} says the debt is half paid.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} looked at {A_nameDef}, then at the gatepost, and said yes.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} was touched, and said no. There's family at {PLACE} who thought {X_objective} lost on the road.

li.label: Tell {X_objective} there's no debt
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} wouldn't hear of payment. They sat together by the gatepost a while instead, and {X_nameDef} went home to {PLACE} promising the colony hadn't heard the last of it.

texts.li: The fever {X_nameDef} carried to the colony's gate has reached {PLACE}, and it's going through the town a street at a time. {X_nameDef} had it once and won't catch it again, so {X_nameDef} is the one who came up the road to ask: the colony pulled one of them through it. Can it spare medicine for the rest?

[nursed] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knows what the fever needs, because {X_nameDef} watched {A_nameDef} do it. It's in {PLACE} now, house after house, and the healer there has run out of everything. {X_nameDef} has come back to the colony to ask for medicine, and for whatever {A_nameDef} can tell {X_objective}.

[worked] The wood {X_nameDef} cut for the colony is still drying by the treeline. Now {X_nameDef} is back at the gate with a different face on: the fever has reached {PLACE}, and the town has run out of medicine.

[nodebt] "You said there was no debt," {X_nameDef} says at the gate. "So I've come to ask a favor instead." The fever {X_nameDef} lived through is going through {PLACE}, and the town's healer has nothing left.

li.label: Send medicine back with {X_objective} (4)
li.outcome: Four doses went into {X_nameDef}'s pack, wrapped in oilcloth, and {X_nameDef} set off for {PLACE} at a run.

li.label: {A_nameDef} tells {X_objective} everything the fever taught
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat {X_nameDef} down and went through it all: cold cloths, clean water, who to keep apart, what to watch for in the second week. {X_nameDef} wrote it down on the back of a feed sack.

li.label: Keep the gate shut until it passes
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} through the gate that the colony couldn't risk it. {X_nameDef} didn't argue, and went back down the road alone.
